classification.difficultyReason: Interpret the mean and amplitude of a supplied cosine model, substitute an exact time and identify recurring minima.

content.prompt: A vertical spring is pulled down and then let go. It bounces back up and down again according to the equation $h=12\cos t+15$, where $h$ is the height of the spring in cm and $t$ is time in seconds. The graph of its motion is shown below for the first 10 seconds.

spec.description: Positive arrowed axes, no grid; t ticks 5 and 10, h ticks 10, 20 and 30. Blue cosine curve begins at 27 and ends rising with an arrow.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied graph remains visible in every edition.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Describe the significance of the 15 in the equation.

answer.short: The mean, or equilibrium, height is $15$ cm.
answer.worked: The spring oscillates about its mean, or equilibrium, height of $15$ cm.

children.label: b
children.prompt: What are the maximum and minimum heights of the spring?

children.label: c
children.prompt: What is the height of the spring after $\pi$ seconds?

children.label: d
children.prompt: At what times will the spring be at its minimum height?

answer.worked: The minimum occurs when $\cos t=-1$. Hence $t=\pi,3\pi,5\pi,\ldots$ seconds.
